checked_claims: The load-bearing chain is: the Borel–Moore localization sequence reduces degree-16 homology to finitely many pure-weight interior terms; published CKgP results cover all but the listed endpoint pairs; a new incidence presentation is supposed to establish CKgP for M_{3,12}; Poincare duality then converts its pure cohomology into W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}. The incidence-to-CKgP step is not proved.

Claim J contains an additional decisive gap not isolated by the attempt: the stack with an ordering of C∩Q is a finite etale ordering cover of the transverse parameter space. CKgP does not ascend along arbitrary finite etale covers. The cited projective-bundle and open-substack lemmas establish CKgP for the unordered base, not for its ordering cover. Thus CKgP of I, required before Proposition 4.2 can descend it to D, remains unsupported.

Claims I and K correctly identify the dependent locus on geometric points: for a smooth plane quartic and twelve distinct markings, the residual degree-zero line bundle has a section exactly when O_C(Γ)≅O_C(3), and the cubic is unique up to scale. However, geometric-point bijectivity does not identify the determinantal scheme structure of D, construct a family-wise inverse, or compare stabilizers.

The proposed non-transverse gap is overstated set-theoretically: markings in M_{3,12} are pairwise distinct, so the unique cubic has reduced intersection divisor Γ and corank cannot exceed one on a smooth connected quartic. Infinitesimal or scheme-structure issues may remain, but no separate geometric stratum of colliding markings lies inside M_{3,12}.

The argument consistently concerns stacks. The lift from F_{4,12} over BPGL_3 to the incidence construction over BSL_3 introduces a μ_3-gerbe, so a map I→D must be constructed as a stack morphism with its stabilizers. Passing silently to geometric points or coarse spaces cannot supply the missing proper representable-by-DM-stacks morphism.

All cited Chow and transfer statements are rational. In particular, Chow invariance for the μ_3-gerbe and averaging over finite automorphism or ordering groups can fail integrally through 3-torsion or primes dividing 12!. No integral conclusion follows.

For dim M_{3,12}=18, the correct duality is H^{BM}_{16}(M_{3,12})≅H^{20}(M_{3,12})(18), hence W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}≅W_{20}H^{20}(18). It is not obtained from W_{16}H^{16}. If CKgP supplied W_{20}H^{20}≅Q(-10)^r, the resulting twist would indeed be Q(8)^r, so the final Tate twist is correct but the intermediate degree is omitted.

In cohomological form, a one-edge boundary Gysin map contributing to H^{20} has source H^{18} of the normalized boundary with twist (-1); an e-edge gluing raises degree by 2e and contributes twist (-e). In homological form the proper pushforward preserves degree. The attempt cites the published right-exact sequence but does not supply the Gysin/Kunneth bookkeeping for its proposed degree-16 induction.

No new spectral-sequence degeneration is actually proved or needed for the local incidence strategy: equation (6.1) is a published weight/localization consequence. Any stronger conclusion from the full weight spectral sequence would require controlling its differentials, which the attempt does not attempt.

For a boundary component M_Γ/Aut(Γ), rational cohomology is obtained by Aut(Γ)-invariants; coinvariants are identified only after averaging over the finite group. Multi-edge weight complexes additionally carry det E(Γ). These operations and signs are absent from the proposed degree-16 induction, although no contrary invariants/coinvariants assertion is made.

If CKgP were established, Lemma 4.3 would give an actual algebraic pure Hodge structure, not merely its semisimplification. A pure rational Hodge structure of type (-8,-8) is actually Q(8)^r. This does not justify an actual l-adic decomposition from statements stated only after semisimplification.

The attempt does not use Chenevier–Lannes predictions, point-count predictions, or conjectural motives as theorems. The supplied survey explicitly records degrees 16, 18, and 20 as open, consistent with the attempt's conditional status.

CKgP alone gives algebraicity and Hodge–Tate purity of the pure piece; it does not give A_*=R_* or tautological generation. Consequently, even a repaired M_{3,12} CKgP argument could support a pure-Tate conclusion but would not extend the published theorem that degree-16 homology is tautological without a separate tautological Chow calculation.

The numerical reduction n≤18-2g for n≥2 is correct despite the stray arithmetic text in Claim A. Relative to the published bounds, the exceptional stable pairs for g≥3 are exactly (3,12), (5,8), (6,6), (7,4), and (8,n) for n=0,1,2; genus 4 contributes none. The attempt treats only (3,12), while all the other residual inputs remain omitted, so it cannot prove a global degree-16 statement.
scope_checks: pure Tate versus algebraic or tautological generation
strongest_attack: Finite-etale ascent failure in Claim J: ordering the twelve intersection points produces a finite etale cover of an open projective-bundle parameter space, but CKgP does not in general ascend along finite etale covers. Therefore I is not shown to have CKgP, so the proposed descent to D and the entire new M_{3,12} base case fail even if stacky properness of I→D is repaired.
